 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226
And 227 Of The Constitution Of India Praying To
Direct The Respondent No.3 I.E., The Tahsildhar,
Devanahalli Taluk To Mutate The Revenue Entries In
The Name Of The Petitioner, In Terms Of Section 129 Of
The Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, In Respect Of
The Admeasuring 1 Acre Of Area In Sy.No.37, Araluru
Village, Channapatna Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk,
Bengaluru And Etc.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Sri.Gopal V. Bailamane, learned counsel is accepts notice for respondent No.2.
2.

Case of the petitioner is that land bearing Sy.No.37 of Araluru Village, Channapatna Hobli,
Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru, admeasuring 1 acre was in unauthorized occupation of father of petitioner namely Kadirappa which was regularized by order dated NC: 2023:KHC:32718 25.04.1984 and a Saguvali Chit in this regard was issued on 26.04.1986.
However, in the revenue records necessary entries were not made.

In the meanwhile respondent-KIADB had issued preliminary notification dated 06.11.2014 and final notification dated 15.11.2018 as per Annexure-A and neither name of the father of petitioner nor name of the petitioner was reflected in the said notification for want of revenue entries in the revenue records.
Consequently, petitioner had initiated proceedings before the Assistant Commissioner seeking entry in the revenue records.
Pursuant thereof the Assistant Commissioner by order dated 24.08.2022 remanded the matter to the Tahsildar to make necessary entries in the revenue records.
Thereafter the petitioner made a representation to the Special Land Acquisition Officer on 26.06.2023 as per Annexure-H seeking compensation in terms of Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act.
It is the grievance of the petitioner that no order has been passed by respondent-SLAO on the representation till date.

After remand of the matter by the Assistant Commissioner to Tahsildar it appears that Tahsildar has sent communication to respondent-SLAO as per Annexure -G seeking Narasimhappa vs State Of Karnataka on 11 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103766661/
2 clarification as to whether the revenue entries could be made in respect of acquired land and compensation be paid, if so, under what provision.
3.

Sri.Gopal V. Bailamane, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 submits that in the fact situation of the matter, given sometime respondent-SLAO would consider the case of the petitioner on merits in accordance with law.
4. Submission is taken on record.

5. Petition is disposed of directing the respondent - SLAO to consider the representation of the petitioner as per Annexure-H and pass appropriate orders within an outer limit of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Needless to state in the process, respondent-SLAO is at liberty to call for records from the concerned revenue department to verify the genuiness or otherwise of claim made by the petitioner.
Petitioner may also be afforded opportunity of personal hearing if need be.

Sd/-
